Prepare annual NIS files

Source: vignettes/articles/prepare-data.Rmd
prepare-data.Rmd
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

Convert the annual Core files

HCUP distributes the Core file as fixed-width ASCII. Unpack the annual archive and pass the .asc file to nis_convert(path, dir). Repeat for each data year using the same private output directory. The supported ASCII layouts use the annual Core filenames and fields. The 2015 ASCII Core file has separate diagnosis and procedure files. Prepare those separately before an analysis that needs the code slots. nis_convert() converts the 2015 ASCII Core file alone. For code-based work, use an annual Stata, SAS, or SPSS input with the code slots already attached.

For Stata (.dta), SAS (.sas7bdat), or SPSS (.sav), the call is the same. Install haven for these formats. Each input must have a numeric YEAR column with one data year. This example converts a Stata file made from invented data.

source <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |> collect()
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpcHihy8/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpcHihy8/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
stata <- file.path(tempdir(), "NIS_2019_Core.dta")
haven::write_dta(source, stata)
annual <- tempfile("nis-annual-")
dir.create(annual)
nis_convert(stata, annual)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpcHihy8/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.

If conversion reports malformed UTF-8, check the source encoding and correct the source or supply its known encoding for a haven format. For example, use encoding = "latin1" for confirmed Latin-1 input. An encoding override cannot repair damaged bytes.

Open the years you need 

nis <- nis_open(annual, years = 2019, check_release = FALSE)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpcHihy8/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
analysis <- nis |> select(nis_vars_design(), AGE, LOS)
colnames(analysis)
#> [1] "YEAR"        "HOSP_NIS"    "NIS_STRATUM" "DISCWT"      "DQTR"       
#> [6] "AGE"         "LOS"
nis |> count(YEAR) |> collect()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>    YEAR     n
#>   <int> <dbl>
#> 1  2019    96

nis_open() returns a DuckDB query. Keep the annual release check on when using complete licensed releases. Compare the release-check warnings with the annual file documentation. Use check_release = FALSE for an intentional extract. Keep projection, flags, and other supported operations before collect(). How easyNIS works

Check that your code fields can be read 

nis |> count(I10_DX1, sort = TRUE) |> head(5) |> collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   I10_DX1     n
#>   <chr>   <dbl>
#> 1 I5022      54
#> 2 J189       42
nis |> count(I10_PR1, sort = TRUE) |> head(5) |> collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   I10_PR1     n
#>   <chr>   <dbl>
#> 1 02703ZZ    48
#> 2 0JH60DZ    48

A query can open before DuckDB reads text from the code fields. Check the diagnosis and procedure columns used in your study. If one fails with malformed UTF-8, reconvert from the correctly encoded source into a new directory and review the release check.

Use nis_open(reader = "arrow") when you need to preserve the source bytes, including malformed UTF-8. easyNIS limits the size of Arrow scan batches to reduce decoded read-ahead across annual files. During a query, it caps Arrow’s CPU worker pool at the DuckDB thread count from when the source was opened. Set options(easyNIS.duckdb_config = list(threads = 4L, memory_limit = "4 GiB")) before opening the data to use a four-thread DuckDB profile. A smaller threads value can reduce scan memory further.

DuckDB’s memory_limit governs its buffer manager. Budget separately for Arrow’s decoded Parquet batches, which depend on the projected columns and file layout, and for the R objects created by collection. Both readers materialize cohort rows in R for nis_design(). Keep only the years and columns needed for the analysis and pass the needed analysis columns in keep. For estimators supported by nis_survey(), leaving the discharge rows in DuckDB avoids materializing the cohort in R.

Join companion files 

needed <- c("HOSP_BEDSIZE", "HOSP_LOCTEACH")
missing <- setdiff(needed, colnames(nis))
missing
#> character(0)

If the result is empty, the requested fields are already in the opened extract. Check their source and data years and use the existing fields. Join only missing fields from a separate companion path.

Prepare annual companion Parquet files with their documented keys. Use nis_join_companion(nis, hospital_path, component = "hospital", columns = all_of(missing)) to add hospital characteristics. Use component = "severity" with the Severity file. Select only fields you need and check coverage after joining. See the companion join example for a complete workflow with invented data.

TOTAL_DISC in the Hospital file counts sampled discharges. The join helper rejects that field. Use weighted discharge estimates for national totals. Years and coding eras
